newsitem.title: USA: Clinton plans two-day trip to Mexico City.
newsitem.headline: Clinton plans two-day trip to Mexico City.

text.p: U.S. President Bill Clinton is planning a two-day visit to Mexico City next month during a week-long trip that will also include stops in Costa Rica and Barbados, White House officials said on Wednesday.

Because Clinton is recovering from knee surgery, he will restrict his May 5-7 visit to Mexico City and its environs, they said. Before the surgery there had been tentative plans for him to visit Mayan ruins elsewhere in Mexico.
He will meet Mexican President Ernesto Zedillo and join him for a news conference. There are plans for him to give a speech while there.
The United States certified Mexico as a U.S. ally in the war against illegal drugs in February despite protests from some members of Congress that Mexico's record was inadequate.

The two countries agreed March 27 on a common strategy to fight drug trafficking. They committed themselves to increase security along their border and to ensure that traffickers could not evade justice in one country by fleeing to the other.
Clinton's anti-drug czar, retired Gen. Barry McCaffrey, traveled to Mexico City Wednesday for talks with Mexico's attorney general and foreign minister.
McCaffrey's spokesman, Bob Weiner, said drug policy would be "a very important issue" on Clinton's agenda during his visit to Mexico.
After Mexico, Clinton will visit to Costa Rica to attend a Central American summit. He then is to travel to Barbados to participate in a Caribbean summit.
